summary.text:
US and European equities advanced, with the Nasdaq up 2.28% and the DAX gaining 1.2%, while Asian markets declined. Nvidia rose 2.87% even as its board weighed CEO Jensen Huang's future amid a deepening scandal. In macroeconomic developments, the UK economy expanded 0.7% in the third quarter, its fastest pace in over two years, while German debt concerns surfaced despite better growth than France.

Treasury yields edged higher. The US dollar index held at 102.938, with the euro falling 0.71% to 1.109 and the yen weakening 0.64% to 159.722. Commodities saw Brent crude rise 0.51% to 93.23 while gold dropped 0.85% to 3966.5. Bitcoin traded down 0.52% at 73577.0391.

Investors are watching for upcoming US inflation and housing data, assessments of US consumer resilience, and the conclusion of Nvidia's extended board meeting.
